headline.text: 7 of 36 operators that transform the store join one kernel: a weighted sum of them applies to every stored item in one shared pass.
headline.denominator: Operators: entries whose class is kernel, pass-per-term or write (36 = 7 + 14 + 15).
headline.beside: The other operators are shown in their classes: pass-per-term 14 (one pass per term in a mix), write 15 (not kernel elements).
headline.reads: All 45 reads answer from the store array in one pass each (CausalReads is the stated exception: one pass per prefix). This is a fact about reads, not part of the score.
headline.why: Reads are not counted in the score: a read answers from the array in one pass by definition, so counting it would measure nothing about superposition. The score asks how many operators that change the store can be summed into one pass.

summary.refusedNote: refused = 0: no operation is refused in every configuration; configuration refusals are in each evidence text.

classes.meaning: Joins a PleromaKernel. The operation is a per-block multiplier (a flag XOR, a left arrangement, a time shift, or Diffuse), or it sums or composes kernels. A kernel applies all of its elements in one pass over the store.

operations.name: Tick
operations.evidence: Ages every item by n ticks in one pass. A time shift is a kernel element. Checked over all combinations of shift, diffusion and count modulo 16.

operations.name: Diffuse
operations.evidence: Equals the two-element kernel (stay with weight a, move one tick with weight b minus a), up to the time scale. Expected counts exact over 600 steps.

operations.name: Apply(PleromaKernel)
operations.evidence: One pass applies every element of the kernel. The result equals the store built from every moved, weighted item, cell for cell and view for view, for kernels of 1, 10, 100 and 1,000 elements and the whole group.

operations.name: PleromaKernel.Add(flagMask, arrangement, timeShift, weight)
operations.evidence: Adds one group element (flag XOR, left arrangement, time shift) with a weight to a kernel. Applying a sum of elements equals the sum of the applies.

operations.name: PleromaKernel.Add(PleromaKernel)
operations.evidence: Sums two kernels of the same shape. Applying the sum equals the sum of the applies.

operations.name: PleromaKernel.Compose
operations.evidence: Composes two kernels block by block. Applying the composition equals applying the two kernels in sequence.

operations.name: PleromaKernel.Adjoint
operations.evidence: Returns the transpose of a kernel, which is again a kernel. The adjoint of the adjoint is the kernel itself, and the adjoint of a composition is the composition of the adjoints.

classes.meaning: Transforms the store in one pass, but moves harmonics rather than scaling them (key relabelling, bit maps, right relabelling, sign flips, per-key or per-tick weights). A weighted mix of different operations of this kind costs one pass per term.

operations.name: RelabelFlags
operations.evidence: The XOR-mask form is a kernel element. A bit permutation is a harmonic permutation and costs one pass per term.

operations.name: RelabelArrangements
operations.evidence: The left-only form is a kernel element. The right side and conjugation are harmonic permutations and cost one pass per term.

operations.name: ShiftKeys
operations.evidence: Shifts every key by a constant in one pass. A key shift is not a kernel element; a weighted mix of key shifts costs one pass per term. Several primes need an explicit key cycle.

operations.name: ScaleKeys
operations.evidence: Relabels every key by a unit (a permutation) or gathers keys by a non-unit, in one pass. Needs the complete key band. A weighted mix costs one pass per term.

operations.name: Frobenius
operations.evidence: Squares every flag word in GF(2^m) for any number of steps, in one pass. A mix with other bit maps costs one pass per term.

operations.name: ShiftRegister
operations.evidence: Steps every flag word through a linear shift register for any number of steps, in one pass. A mix with other bit maps costs one pass per term.

operations.name: Apply(FlagOperator)
operations.evidence: Applies a signed permutation of the flag words in one pass. Signs of weight two or more need the flag spectrum. Signs are not kernel elements.

operations.name: MapTimes
operations.evidence: Applies any map of the ticks in one pass. Needs complete time groups (refuses a lone s = 1 line). Period up to 4096. A mix of maps costs one pass per map.

operations.name: ModulateKeys
operations.evidence: Multiplies every key harmonic by a phase, in one pass; the exact partner of ShiftKeys. Refused on a check-prime store.

operations.name: MultiplyKeys
operations.evidence: Applies a weight to every key count in one pass. Weights are convolutions in harmonic space; a mix of different weightings costs one pass per term.

operations.name: MultiplyTimes
operations.evidence: Applies a weight to every tick in one pass. A mix of different weightings costs one pass per term.

operations.name: ApplyBank
operations.evidence: Applies a bank of shifted diagonals in one pass. A sum of banks costs one pass per term.

operations.name: PleromaKernel.Graded
operations.evidence: Builds the generators of the sign-graded tower as signed permutations of the flag words. Those generators act one pass per term.

operations.name: FlagOperator.Apply(counts)
operations.evidence: Applies a signed permutation to a count vector in one pass. Signs are not kernel elements.

classes.meaning: An operator that transforms the store and is not a kernel element: it changes the state of the store it is called on, or it returns a new store holding transformed counts. Covers every stored item in one pass, without a kernel.

operations.name: Bind
operations.evidence: Binds two stores in one pass (group convolution). A many-item other store applies its mix of shifts in one pass. Refused with several primes.

operations.name: CombineCycles
operations.evidence: Joins two coprime complete key cycles into one in one pass. Refused for stores with a relation face, a check prime or reserved keys.

operations.name: Restrict
operations.evidence: Keeps the items whose flag word satisfies a 0/1 predicate, in one pass.

operations.name: Add(Pleroma)
operations.evidence: Adds another store's cells in one pass (multiset union). Exact.

operations.name: Subtract(Pleroma)
operations.evidence: Subtracts another store's cells in one pass. Exact signed difference.

operations.name: MergeProjection
operations.evidence: Merges the cells of a projection back into the full store in one pass. Refused for relation faces, check-prime and reserved-key stores.

operations.name: FromCounts
operations.evidence: Builds a dense page from a count vector in one transform.

operations.name: AddCounts
operations.evidence: Adds a count vector to a dense page in one transform.

operations.name: AddFlagCounts
operations.evidence: Adds a flag histogram under one key in one Walsh transform.

operations.name: Project
operations.evidence: Copies the cells of a smaller shadow store for the chosen faces. Relation faces are not carried.

operations.name: ProjectFlags
operations.evidence: Gathers chosen flag bits into a smaller shadow store, exactly.

operations.name: Repair
operations.evidence: Rebuilds lost harmonics from the reserved keys, or rebuilds the whole store from the syndromes. Exact.

operations.name: MapCounts
operations.evidence: Applies any function to every key count in one pass. Non-linear, so not a kernel element.

operations.name: Support
operations.evidence: The set of keys with a nonzero count, in one pass.

operations.name: Hadamard
operations.evidence: Pointwise product of two stores' key counts, in one pass. Shapes must match.

reads.name: Eliminate
reads.evidence: Solves in one shot for the GF(2) parity rule that fits every stored example. Inputs of at most 15 bits.

reads.name: IsIndependent
reads.evidence: Tests in exact integers whether joint counts equal the product of their marginals.

reads.name: Syndrome
reads.evidence: Counts stored words per Hamming syndrome in one read. Needs flag bits 3, 7 or 15.

reads.name: Sample
reads.evidence: Draws one value with probability count over total in one read. The store is not changed.

reads.name: SampleKey
reads.evidence: Draws one key of a dense page with probability count over total.

reads.name: TimeSpectrum
reads.evidence: Reads each key's exact tick histogram in one decode. Needs the TimeSpectrum option. Returns null past key capacity.

reads.name: TimeMap
reads.evidence: Reads one tick per key, or a mix, in one read. Needs the TimeSpectrum option.

reads.name: TryFindConflicts
reads.evidence: Lists the keys that carry more than one tick, flag word or arrangement, in one read. Needs item lines.

reads.name: TryKeys
reads.evidence: Reads every key's total count in one decode. Refuses past KeyCapacity distinct keys.

reads.name: TryItems
reads.evidence: Reads whole items in one decode when each key holds one value per face. Refuses past KeyCapacity distinct keys.

reads.name: Flags
reads.evidence: Exact count of every flag word, read from the flag slice.

reads.name: Near
reads.evidence: Counts the items whose flag word lies within a Hamming radius of a query.

reads.name: Nearest
reads.evidence: Returns the stored words nearest a query, with their distance.

reads.name: Arrangements
reads.evidence: Exact count of every arrangement, indexed by ArrangementIndex.

reads.name: SignBalance
reads.evidence: Even minus odd arrangement count.

reads.name: Times
reads.evidence: Exact count at every tick.

reads.name: JointCounts
reads.evidence: Exact joint counts over the chosen faces, read from the joint slice. Needs the faces in JointFaces.

reads.name: CountWhere
reads.evidence: Counts the items whose flag word satisfies a predicate, in one read of the flag slice. Accepts any predicate or a compiled one.

reads.name: CountWhereByTime
reads.evidence: Counts per tick for a predicate, read from the joint slice. Needs JointFaces with Flags and Time.

reads.name: CountWhereByArrangement
reads.evidence: Counts per arrangement for a predicate, read from the joint slice. Needs JointFaces with Flags and Order.

reads.name: BitCounts
reads.evidence: Count of stored items with each flag bit set, in one read.

reads.name: FlagParity
reads.evidence: XOR of every stored flag word, in one read.

reads.name: Attend
reads.evidence: From one contraction of the store: the exact count of matched items per value, shares summing to 1, and the parity of the match count.

reads.name: Density
reads.evidence: Graded density at a key. Needs the continuous component.

reads.name: Similarity
reads.evidence: Graded similarity of two keys. Needs the continuous component.

reads.name: FadedTimes
reads.evidence: Age-faded tick weights. Needs the continuous component.

reads.name: RelationPairs
reads.evidence: Lists the key pairs that carry relations with a tag.

reads.name: ReadLoop
reads.evidence: Linear read of a loop: the signed sum of offsets around it, from the relation cells.

reads.name: Holonomy
reads.evidence: Winding of a loop modulo RelationModulus.

reads.name: Frustration
reads.evidence: Parity of a loop's offset sum.

reads.name: Current
reads.evidence: Sign of the steady-state circulation around a loop of rates.

reads.name: Total
reads.evidence: Total count of the store, read in one pass.

reads.name: Counts
reads.evidence: Exact count at every key slot in one transform. Complete key band only.

reads.name: CountWhereKey
reads.evidence: Sum of a key predicate over a dense page, in one read. Complete key band only.

reads.name: MinKey
reads.evidence: Smallest key with a nonzero count, from the dense page.

reads.name: MaxKey
reads.evidence: Largest key with a nonzero count, from the dense page.

reads.name: KeyAtRank
reads.evidence: Key at a given rank in the count order, from the dense page.

reads.name: InnerProduct
reads.evidence: Exact equi-join sum of two dense pages, in one read.

reads.name: CountsInto
reads.evidence: Reads a whole dense page into a buffer in one transform.

reads.name: Verify
reads.evidence: Checks the syndromes at the reserved keys. Exact.

reads.name: VerifyCheck
reads.evidence: Checks the mirror in the check prime against the main cells.

reads.name: TimeWeightedCounts
reads.evidence: Exact time-weighted counts per key for a fading weight, in one read.

reads.name: CausalReads
reads.evidence: Reads after every prefix of a sequence. One read per prefix; the prefixes are not one pass.

reads.name: FlagInnerProduct
reads.evidence: Exact inner product of two stores' flag slices.

reads.name: ToComplex
reads.evidence: One-way floating-point export of the stored cells.

readsMeaning: Returns a value (a count, an array, a key, an item list, a boolean, a distribution) and leaves the store unchanged. Answers from the store array in one pass, except where the evidence says otherwise (CausalReads takes one pass per prefix).

plumbing.meaning: No transform of the stored items: single-item input, index conversion, operator construction, raw persistence, equality, copies. Excluded from both the operator count and the read count.

notBuilt.name: R8b contradiction location
notBuilt.evidence: Locating the contradiction on a relation face is not implemented.

construction.brick: Reed-Solomon and BCH syndrome decoding (Reed and Solomon 1960; Bose and Ray-Chaudhuri 1960)
construction.alone: Recovers up to K distinct symbols exactly from 2K+1 power sums, and refuses beyond that.
construction.pleroma: The key view: `TryKeys` and `TryItems` read the key line by syndrome decoding and refuse past `KeyCapacity`.
construction.proof: Keys exact in 30 of 30 trials at 16 keys, and refused in 30 of 30 trials at 17 and 20 keys.

construction.alone: Finds the shortest recurrence that generates a syndrome sequence.
construction.pleroma: The decoder of the key view (`CycleDecoder`), with a re-encode check on every decode. CycleHologram uses the same decoder.
construction.proof: CycleHologram decodes exactly across the capacity sweeps; the Pleroma key view and CycleHologram agree on one decoder.

construction.brick: PinSketch and minisketch set reconciliation (Talbot et al. 2012; Poinsot et al. 2017)
construction.alone: A sketch sized to the difference of two sets decodes that difference.
construction.pleroma: Replica reconciliation: two holograms subtract exactly and the signed difference decodes. The Pleroma subtracts exactly, and its key view decodes the difference up to `KeyCapacity`.
construction.proof: CycleHologram decodes the exact signed multiset difference across the tested cases; Pleroma `Subtract` is exact across a sequence of merge, tick, relabel and serialize steps.

construction.alone: The spectrum of a Boolean function on flag words, from which the count under any predicate is one inner product.
construction.pleroma: `CountWhere`, `CountWhereByTime` and `CountWhereByArrangement` count the items under any predicate of the flag word in one read; `Attend` uses the same contraction.
construction.proof: Predicate counts equal direct counting in 1,515 of 1,515 cases on three fields.

construction.brick: Group convolution (Fourier analysis on finite groups)
construction.alone: The product of two group-algebra elements is a convolution, and in the Fourier domain it is a product on each block.
construction.pleroma: `Bind` (keys add, flags XOR, arrangements compose, ticks add, counts multiply) and kernel `Apply` (a product on each block of stored harmonics).
construction.proof: `Bind` equals the store of all pairs, cell for cell and view for view, in 35 of 35 cases across five shapes. `Apply` equals the store of moved items, cell for cell, for kernels of 1, 10, 100 and 1,000 elements and for the whole group.

construction.alone: Joins residues modulo coprime moduli into one residue modulo their product.
construction.pleroma: `CombineCycles` joins two coprime complete key cycles into one key space. Each pair of keys becomes the key with both residues.
construction.proof: `CombineCycles` equals the store of Chinese-remainder pairs in 12 of 12 cases on two fields.

construction.alone: The syndrome of a word locates a single error.
construction.pleroma: `Syndrome` counts the stored words per Hamming syndrome, for 3, 7 or 15 flag bits.
construction.proof: All 112 single errors of Hamming(7,4) are located, and all 336 double errors are sent to a wrong third position.

construction.alone: A linear recurrence over GF(2) with a period set by its polynomial.
construction.pleroma: `ShiftRegister` steps every stored flag word through the register, for any number of steps in one pass.
construction.proof: The stepped store equals the store of stepped words. The recorded periods are 255 and 63 for primitive polynomials.

construction.brick: Frobenius map on GF(2^m) (finite field arithmetic)
construction.alone: Squaring in a binary field is a linear map on its elements.
construction.pleroma: `Frobenius` squares every stored flag word modulo a polynomial, for any number of steps in one pass.
construction.proof: The store equals the store of squared words. Its order on GF(2^8) is exactly 8.

construction.brick: Time diffusion on a cycle (Markov chains)
construction.alone: A walk that stays with some probability and otherwise moves one step.
construction.pleroma: `Diffuse` runs the walk on every item at once and gives exact expected counts, scaled by `TimeScale`. `Tick` ages every item exactly.
construction.proof: Expected counts are exact over 20 steps on two fields, and the recorded run is exact over 600 steps.

construction.brick: Holographic Reduced Representations: binding and bundling (Plate 1995)
construction.alone: Key-value pairs superposed by a sum and read back by correlation. The read is approximate, and its noise grows with load.
construction.pleroma: The continuous component is the bundle. `Density`, `Similarity` and `FadedTimes` read it with graded similarity. The exact cells are read by decoding.
construction.proof: The continuous bundle is a slice of the store, and its similarity is the kernel of the component (`PleromaContinuousTests`, CF1).
